analysis:
No qualifying findings in the supplied units.

NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift is a new internal actor that serves inline base64 consumer images (A-001, TB-007, TB-003/T-050).
- Accepted input: only PNG/JPEG data URIs, at most 16 images, body at most 8 MiB, and template at most 1 MiB. Tools, response_format, logprobs and prompt_cache_key are rejected. There is no URL fetching.
- The decode path appears to touch no temp files, so the T-050 plaintext-on-disk class is not reintroduced.
- Execution calls bridge.submitTokenized with cacheScope "" and cacheEnabled false, so it creates no prefix-cache entries and does not touch the T-041 cross-tenant TTFT channel or at-rest artifacts.
- Memory admission goes through VisionMemoryGate: an ingress reservation (lines 70-78) before JSON/base64 expansion, then a media reservation at lines 83-84. Reservations are released after the work task completes (113-121). They are deliberately left unreleased when hasRetainedImageFault, which quarantines the owner, so this is not a leak.
- Concurrency: the one-active-request guard is set synchronously before the first suspension (lines 40-41, 68-69, 122). drain() cancels and awaits the active task.
- Arithmetic: overflow-checked sums are used in preparationQuote. encodedPlan multiplies grid.width * grid.height * 24 without an overflow check. I assumed the grid is bounded by NemotronSuperImagePreprocessing and NemotronSuperImageDecode.inspect, which are outside the supplied files.

EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift adds an optional schedulerPolicy closure to prepareProductionBackend. It mutates the resolved scheduler config in servingPolicy (lines 206-216) after productionServingPolicy runs, for both the contiguous and paged paths.

EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (lines 87-94, 113-115):
- Calibrated Nemotron prefill limits clamp prefillChunkSize and mixedStepPrefillTokenCap, and disable solo striping, inside productionSchedulerConfig.
- configureNativeQwen4Batching now rejects a non-positive calibrated limit.

For the next pass: the schedulerPolicy closure runs after the calibrated clamp, so a caller could widen the clamp. The comment at Configuration lines 87-89 claims overrides cannot widen it, but the supplied evidence shows no caller of the new parameter. I also could not confirm that productionServingPolicy does not apply profile overrides after productionSchedulerConfig. The workspace bound in the comment is a memory-safety control rather than a trust-boundary control. Callers and tests are unseen, so this is an unverified contract, not a finding.
